text:
alex_pm: Quick thread to lock down "burst credit expiry" behavior before we write the RFC. Customers want short bursts but also predictable billing. Need decision on decay vs hard-expiry.

rachel_prod: Quick context: three customers asked for carryover of unused credits between weekly billing windows. They want some buffer for bursty days.

marco_eng: Two engineering approaches: (A) Hard expiry: credits awarded per billing window and drop to zero at window end. Simpler billing, simpler enforcement. (B) Sliding decay: credits exponentially decay over time (e.g., half-life 3d) so unused credits thinned but not lost immediately. More complex but softer UX.

nina_oncall: From ops POV, hard expiry is cleaner for runbooks. Sliding decay means more edge cases, and accounting for partial-window allocations will complicate incident triage.

evan_sales: Customers prefer sliding decay. "Hard expiry" language is a dealbreaker for two pilots unless we offer a grace add-on. Sales suggests default decay with optional hard-reset for enterprise contracts.

marco_eng: Implementation notes: token-bucket per tenant remains, but refill logic changes. For sliding decay we store last_refill_ts and decay_factor. We'll emit billing events with remaining_credit snapshot at window boundary. Cost impact: decay keeps lower net utilization than hard expiry because credits carry forward.

rachel_prod: UX ask: add "credit-preview" in Console so customers can see projected carryover and cost impact before window end. Also show a "use-or-lose" flag per account.

nina_oncall: Alerting: add a pulse metric when a tenant switches from "carryover" to "depleted" state mid-window --- that's often when we get pages. Also add runbook step: if depletion rate > 3x baseline for 10m, escalate to oncall + account owner.

evan_sales: Pricing note: we can upsell a "stable-burst" tier that guarantees hard carryover for a price. That avoids the softness customers dislike.

marco_eng: Edge cases to call out in RFC: long single bursts (minutes) that exceed bucket_size, simultaneous cross-pool bursts, and retroactive adjustments (refunds) if billing event misfires. Need a tolerant enforcement window to avoid immediate throttles during distro delays.

rachel_prod: Proposed decision: default = sliding decay (half-life 72h) + console preview + opt-out flag for hard-expiry at account level; upsell: guaranteed carryover add-on. Launch criteria = telemetry for credit use, billing snapshot export, clear Console messaging, and oncall runbook.

nina_oncall: OK but require a simulated canary with 10 pilot tenants and a stress test showing bounded alert rate before GA. Also need cost model showing expected Dedicated pool occupancy delta.

marco_eng: Example config we'll include in doc: 
```
burst_credit: 
  policy: sliding_decay
  half_life_seconds: 259200  # 72h
  bucket_capacity_seconds: 60
  max_burst_per_request_seconds: 30
  enforcement_grace_seconds: 5
```

evan_sales: Can we surface a simple SDK flag for signing up: `account.burst_policy = "carryover|expire"` so onboarding is low-friction?

marco_eng: Yup. Router will consult account metadata. No infra change required.

alex_pm: Decision captured: go with Rachel's proposal (sliding decay default + opt-out hard-expiry + upsell). Next steps: Marco write RFC and include perf sims (EOD Fri), Nina provide canary runbook and alert thresholds (Mon), Evan prepare upsell pricing and language (next Tue).

ops-bot: job started: infra/credit-sim -> perf (by marco_eng)

alex_pm: Thanks everyone. I'll pull this into the roadmap doc and schedule RFC review.
